1.explanation: To support the new inverse hover/active link states we need to:  1) Add `export const linkInverseHover` and `export const linkInverseActive` with the correct color values to each theme module (white.js, g10.js, g100.js).  2) Add the token names 'linkInverseHover' and 'linkInverseActive' to the `colors` and/or interactive token lists in packages/themes/src/tokens.js so that formatTokenName and the generated CSS variables (`--cds-link-hover-inverse`, `--cds-link-inverse-active`) will be registered. Without these additions the React UI cannot reference those CSS variables and the link hover/active colors on inverse backgrounds remain incorrect.
1.bug_scenario: When rendering tooltips, pop-overs, and notifications on an inverse (dark/high-contrast) surface, the hover and active colors for inline links are coming out wrong (or falling back) because the new inverse interactive tokens — $link-inverse-hover and $link-inverse-active — haven’t been added to our theme modules or to the tokens registry. In the screenshot you can see that on light inverse surfaces (white and g10) hover should be blue-30 (#a6c8ff) and active gray-10 (#f4f4f4), and on dark inverse surfaces (g90/g100) hover should be blue-70 (#0043ce) and active gray-100 (#161616). Those CSS custom properties (--cds-link-hover-inverse, --cds-link-inverse-active) simply don’t exist yet.

2.explanation: The theme files (g10.js, g100.js, white.js) currently only export `inverseLink` but lack dedicated exports for inverse‐link hover and active states (e.g. `linkInverseHover`, `linkInverseActive`). Without those constants, the CSS custom properties `--cds-link-hover-inverse` and `--cds-link-inverse-active` aren’t generated. In tokens.js, the `colors` array and the `tokens` export drive which properties are emitted to CSS, and `formatTokenName` controls their naming. Because the inverse‐hover and inverse‐active link tokens aren’t listed there, no CSS variables exist for them. Adding the new token names to the `colors` array and exporting matching constants in each theme file (and letting `formatTokenName` generate their dashed names) will define `--cds-link-hover-inverse` and `--cds-link-inverse-active` so the interactive link colors render correctly in both light and dark inverse contexts.
2.bug_scenario: In the inverse theme (g10, g100, white) tooltip/pop-over examples the interactive “Learn more” link is using undefined or fallback CSS variables—`--cds-link-hover-inverse` and `--cds-link-inverse-active`—so on hover and active the link color is incorrect (e.g. wrong blue or gray). The images show that hover in light theme should be Blue 30 (#a6c8ff) and in dark theme Blue 70 (#0043ce), and active in light theme Gray 10 (#f4f4f4) and in dark theme Gray 100 (#161616), but those tokens don’t exist yet.
